claims.text: FeCoNiCrAl gas-atomized powder with a 15–45 μm size range previously produced high-quality coatings with the HVAF-M3 configuration.
Increasing the HVAF-i7 spray distance to approximately 300–350 mm will increase particle velocity.
Changing spray distance can alter the oxide content of a high-entropy-alloy coating.
The 300–350 mm spray-distance range will increase deposition efficiency on the HVAF-i7 torch.
Higher particle velocity will reduce particle drop-off and in-flight oxidation.
Higher particle velocity will increase particle impact kinetic energy.
Greater impact kinetic energy will improve splat flattening and interlamellar bonding.
The intervention will promote in-flight particle cohesion and formation of a denser microstructure.
Improved deposition efficiency and inter-splat bonding will permit a thicker coating without loss of coating integrity.
The optimized HVAF-i7 condition will produce a substantially thicker coating than the 15–45 μm-feedstock HVAF-M3 baseline.
The thicker HVAF-i7 coating will remain dense and adherent while retaining similarly minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
Oxide formation during spraying can change the residual particle-core composition and destabilize phases.
The intervention should remain effective during oxidizing thermal-barrier service at temperatures of at least 800 °C.
The intervention should be applicable inside geometries having internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
Effectiveness is conditional on the higher-velocity condition not causing excessive oxidation or loss of adhesion.
The quantitative thickness increase and the balance between deposition efficiency and oxidation remain uncertain pending experiments.

contradictions.description: The proposed intervention is specified for an HVAF-i7 torch, whereas the conditions describe deposition under HVOF spraying. These are distinct process designations.
The predicted outcome is relative to the HVAF-M3 baseline, but the experiment varies only HVAF-i7 spray distance and does not explicitly include an HVAF-M3 control, making the comparator ambiguous.
